message:
fix(viewer): never forget an abandoned identity -- drop the rejected capacity eviction and the unsettled generation retirement

Codex rejected "drop the oldest record when the list is full" twice: forgetting an identity means
accepting it again, which is the defect the tombstone exists to prevent, and documenting it as a
bounded hole does not make it safe. Retiring entries when a delivery of another generation arrives
is not settled either -- the assembler must not follow a late packet's generation, and nothing
calls Reset() from the receive path today. Both come out.

What remains is the confirmed part: no time-to-live, and an entry is retired when delivery has
passed that seq in its own generation, where the ordinary stale guard takes over. Abandoning many
identities with no delivery in between now simply keeps them all; that case is marked UNFINISHED
and RELEASE-BLOCKING where it is enforced, and the saturation design that closes it is being
confirmed. The unit test asserts the new contract: twenty give-ups, twenty identities remembered,
the first as much as the last.

The A06 early-return path is still not covered by an executed regression; the approved fake
transform seam and how it drives the stage path come next. history #421.
